title: 25-storey tower proposed at 83-87 Weber Street East
subtitle: Late height-for-affordability offer, tenant relocation, parking concerns, Dumfries Avenue traffic calming, Morrison Road holding provision.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended that Council adopt an Official Plan amendment and approve a zoning change for a 25-storey mixed-use rental building at 83-87 Weber Street East, near the Frederick and Queen transit stops {{vote:m3}}. The committee also recommended that staff talk with the applicant about more density, affordable housing and other community benefits, and report back by the October 16 Council meeting {{vote:m4}}.

At the meeting the developer offered to go up to 32 storeys, which would mean about 434 units. In return it offered 26 units at 20% below market rent, more energy-efficient design with no natural gas, and adaptable suites. Neighbouring and current residents raised concerns about parking, drop-off space, green space and displacement. The developer said it would help tenants relocate.

The committee also recommended starting a traffic calming review for Dumfries Avenue between Stirling Avenue North and Edna Street {{vote:m1}}, and lifting a holding provision at 7 Morrison Road {{vote:m2}}. These are recommendations, and Council makes the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment, to be sent to the Region of Waterloo for approval, and approving the zoning change for a 25-storey mixed-use building {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Staff to negotiate density and affordable housing
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adding a direction that staff engage the applicant on additional density, affordable housing and community benefits and report back by October 16 {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended starting a traffic calming review for Dumfries Avenue between Stirling Avenue North and Edna Street in 2023 {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended approving a zoning amendment to remove Holding Provision 42H from 7 Morrison Road {{vote:m2}}.

debate: A delegate from a neighbouring counselling organization said the building was needed but too large for the site. Their concerns were a minimal setback, no place for taxi, delivery or moving stops off Weber Street, very little parking, and no green space.

Staff replied that the parking rate follows Council-approved rates for the urban growth centre and that the City has nearby parking capacity. They said the building would be set back from the sidewalk, with on-site vehicle access and a loading space. Staff added that the area has a parkland shortage but no acquisition plan yet.

A tenant of one of the existing buildings asked about relocation. Councillors asked whether rents would be comparable and whether a transition period could be offered. The developer promised notice, support and an open process, and said it would talk with tenants.

Several councillors objected to a height increase raised two weeks before Council decides, saying it weakens public trust since community meetings covered 25 storeys. Staff said late changes strain their workload and they would prefer complete applications. Supporters said the housing crisis justified acting now.

One councillor opposed the amendment, saying the process was being undermined. Another asked that a non-profit housing provider be considered to manage the affordable units, for accountability over the affordability period.
